title: Relay Repair Round
summary: The Driftline's relay net is going deaf at the edges — the pan relay, the east-gate relay, and the overlook mast are all running on cells older than most couriers. Swap the charged drops at each relay, then climb to the moorage mast and re-sync the net before the evening chatter window. Radios are the only road that never gets weather, and it's our road.

objectives.label: Swap the cell drops at the old pan relay
Swap the cell drops at the east-gate relay
Swap the cell drops at the overlook mast
Re-sync the net at the moorage mast

offer.text: Housekeeping, kid. Our relay net's going crusty — three relays around the flats running on cells I installed when you were a rumour. Fresh drops are staged at each one; swap them, then re-sync at the moorage mast before the evening window.
The Driftline's radios are powered by cells as old as me and the only maintenance plan was hoping?
The maintenance plan was *paying attention*, and now you're it. Welcome to infrastructure, kid. It's underneath everything and nobody writes songs about it except the Choir, and theirs hiss.

accept.text: Pan relay first — it's the deafest. The drops are painted amber, half-buried on purpose; sand insulates better than our mud-plugs and won't accept compliments. Tap each relay twice after the swap: once for the wake, once for respect.

Station. You are repairing the *other* voices' roads. That is neighbourly. When the net sings again, the static between stations will be ever so slightly lonelier, and I will pretend not to have a preference.
One more thing — the overlook mast leans. It has leaned for forty years. It is *committed* to leaning. Do not straighten it, the Guild has tried and the mast won.

complete.text: Net's sync'd, chatter window's loud, and the evening gossip just cross-crossed the flats clean for the first time all season. That's you, kid. Nobody will ever know. That's the job.
I fixed three radios and my reward is everyone getting to complain more clearly.
The finest reward infrastructure offers. Bank it. And kid — when I was riding, fixing the net was how I learned the flats. You've now touched every good sightline we own. File that away.
